title: How canal locks work
examples: How do canal locks change the water height?
What part of the lock controls the water flow?
Is the water always the same height in the lock?

explain.say: A canal lock has two main parts you should know about.
The chamber is the box where the boat sits safely.
The gates are strong barriers that can open or close.
The water level changes by letting water in or out.
To lift a boat uphill, the lock fills with water.

items: Step 1: Gates open to higher water
Step 3: Boat rises with the water

explain.say: In real life, canal locks help boats cross different heights.

faq.q: How does the lock know when to stop filling?
faq.a: The lock has mechanisms that stop the water flow when the right level is reached. It is controlled by the sluice gates.
asks: How is the water level managed?

faq.q: Do the gates open all at once?
faq.a: No, the gates are opened carefully to allow the water to enter or leave slowly. This controlled opening is important for safety.
asks: What is the opening process like?

faq.q: Does the boat have to move when the water is rising?
faq.a: No, the boat stays inside the chamber while the water level changes around it. The water does most of the work.
asks: Does the boat need to push anything?
What should the boat do during the lift?

faq.q: Are canal locks only used for boats?
faq.a: While primarily for boats, the principle of changing water levels is used in other engineering projects. It manages water flow across different elevations.
asks: Can locks be used for other things?

faq.q: What is the difference between the upper and lower gates?
faq.a: The upper gates connect to the higher water level, and the lower gates connect to the lower water level. They work together to seal the chamber.
asks: Which gates are at the top?
How are the two ends different?

facts: Canal locks use chambers to hold boats.
Gates are strong barriers that seal the water.
Water levels are changed by letting water in or out.
The process allows boats to move between different heights.

quiz.say: What structure holds the boat while the water level changes?
quiz.show: The boat sits in the chamber.
quiz.why: The chamber is the box designed to hold the boat safely during the water level change.

wrong.1: The upper gates are just the barriers at the high end, not the holding area.
wrong.2: The sluice gate controls the water, but it is not where the boat sits.
wrong.3: The canal is the whole waterway, not the specific area for the boat.

quiz.say: If a boat needs to go to a higher level, what happens to the water inside the lock?

options.show: The gates must open to the lower side.
options.say: The gates must open to the lower side.

options.show: The chamber fills with water from the higher side.
options.say: The chamber fills with water from the higher side.

options.show: The boat has to be pulled by a winch.
options.say: The boat has to be pulled by a winch.

quiz.why: To lift the boat, the water level inside the chamber must rise to match the higher side.

wrong.0: Opening to the lower side would lower the boat, which is the opposite of what is needed.
wrong.2: Draining out would lower the boat, not lift it to a higher level.
wrong.3: The lock uses water pressure, not physical pulling, to move the boat.

quiz.say: Which part of the lock controls the rate of water entering or leaving?
quiz.why: The sluice gate is the specific mechanism that regulates the flow, making the change safe.

wrong.0: The boat is carried by the water, it does not control the water flow.
wrong.2: The chamber is the space, not the control mechanism for the water flow.
wrong.3: The upper gates are barriers, but the sluice gate controls the opening.
